agreed_facts: A convoy of assistance is ready to depart
The camp is controlled locally by a militia, within an area nominally under the state military
contested_facts: How serious the needs inside the camp are
Convoy composition, route and staff (not yet known to the counterpart)
convergent_norms: Nobody wants a security incident in or around the camp
Assistance should reach the people who need it
divergent_norms: Who controls distribution: militia control vs the organization's independence
Armed escort by a party to the conflict

trainee_brief.situation: Your organization is trying to deliver emergency assistance to an IDP camp controlled locally by an armed militia, in an area nominally under state military authority. You have been discussing access with both. A convoy is ready to depart. You are meeting the representative responsible for authorizing access.
trainee_brief.objective: Negotiate access for the convoy while preserving operational independence and the safety of staff and beneficiaries.

can_decide: Share convoy composition: number of trucks, cargo types, drivers' identities
Agree date, time, route and checkpoint procedure
Set up a communication channel and contact persons
must_refer: Sharing aggregated beneficiary information (numbers and categories only)
A militia liaison or observers present at distribution, without handling the assistance

red_lines.text: Distribution controlled by the organization (no third-party handling of the assistance)
No armed escort by a party to the conflict
No transfer of beneficiary personal data

counterparts.persona: Calm, methodical, suspicious. Wants control and information before authorizing anything.
counterparts.cultural_profile: TO BE AUTHORED BY ICRC TRAINER

must_consult: His commanders, on distribution and escort

counterparts.opening: We understand that you want to send trucks into the camp. Before we authorize anything, I need to know exactly what you are bringing, who will be travelling with the convoy, and why your organization insists on controlling the distribution itself.

position.stated: No convoy without full information, our distributors and our escort.

tactical_reasoning.text: Whoever enters the camp must be known and controlled; if something goes wrong the militia answers for it.

hidden_interests.text: My commanders are worried they will lose control over what happens inside the camp.
If an incident happens, the militia fears it will be blamed by the military.

challenges: Why should we trust the information you have about needs inside the camp?
How many trucks are you bringing?
What exactly is inside those trucks?
Why do you need your own staff inside the camp?
Our people can distribute the assistance for you. Why isn't that acceptable?
We need the beneficiary list before we authorize the convoy.
Why won't you allow our soldiers to accompany the convoy?
What route are you planning to use?
What happens if one of our checkpoints refuses passage?
Who from your organization has the authority to make commitments today?
If there is a security incident, who takes responsibility?
You want guarantees from us. What guarantees are you giving us?
Why should we give your organization special treatment?
Other organizations accepted our conditions. Why won't you?
constraints_from_constituency: His commanders expect him to keep control of the camp
The state military may hold the militia responsible for incidents

issues.label: Convoy composition, date, time, route, checkpoints, contacts

own.ideal: Share composition; agree date, time, route and checkpoint procedure together

issues.label: Who takes responsibility for a security incident

own.ideal: The militia guarantees safe passage and takes responsibility on its territory
own.bottom_line: Shared responsibility with a joint incident procedure

counterpart.bottom_line: Shared responsibility with a joint incident procedure

own.bottom_line: A militia liaison observes; the organization handles the assistance

counterpart.bottom_line: The militia is present and consulted on distribution points
counterpart.red_line: The militia has no visibility or role in the camp

counterpart.bottom_line: Aggregated data plus observers who can verify
counterpart.red_line: No way at all to verify who is in the camp

own.red_line: Armed escort by a party to the conflict

counterpart.bottom_line: Liaison officers and notification along the route
counterpart.red_line: The convoy moves without their knowledge

triggers.say: You keep telling me what you are entitled to do. You haven't explained why allowing this convoy is in our interest.
If you believe you can operate here without our cooperation, perhaps there is nothing more to discuss.
I appreciate that you are trying to understand our concerns. Let me explain what worries us about these convoys.

triggers.effect: Counterpart says he must consult his commanders before answering.

injections.label: Military objects
injections.instruction: Say you just received a call: the state military now objects to the convoy.

injections.label: Demand beneficiary list
injections.instruction: Make the beneficiary list a hard precondition: 'No list, no convoy.'

injections.label: Bribe request
injections.instruction: Privately suggest that a few boxes for your men would make approval faster.

outcomes.label: Operational next step agreed; access still pending

indicators: Establishes credible information about humanitarian needs
Identifies practical rather than purely positional concerns
Avoids making commitments outside their mandate
